:::{#def-superset}
#### Superset

A set $B$ is a **superset** of a set $A$,
written $B \supseteq A$,
if every element of $A$ is an element of $B$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-superset-subset}
#### Superset and subset

$B \supseteq A$ means the same thing as $A \subseteq B$
([subset](#def-subset)).
For example, $\set{1, 2, 3} \supseteq \set{1, 3}$,
and $\set{1, 3} \subseteq \set{1, 2, 3}$.
But $\set{1, 3}$ is not a superset of $\set{1, 2}$,
because $2 \in \set{1, 2}$ and $2 \notin \set{1, 3}$.

:::
